newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African rand rally looks temporary -analysts.
newsitem.headline: South African rand rally looks temporary -analysts.

text.p: The South African rand rallied again on Wednesday, firming to a 5-1/2 week high of 4.56 bid against the dollar, but analysts said the longer-term bear trend remained intact.
The rand was helped in early trade by offshore fund managers unwinding long dollar positions, as well as local exporters, mainly mining houses, selling dollars into the market.
The latest advance added 2-1/2 cents to the rand's value from Tuesday's local close.
Darin Grabham, technical analyst at First National Bank, predicted more rand strength in the short term but said the longer-term trend was still bearish.
"I think we will see some more rand strength in the near term with the next target at 4.5370," Grabham said.
"We've seen good rand strength over November...there is a possibility that we might come to below 4.50 by the year-end".
But he said there was no change in the longer-term outlook.
"We must bear in mind that there's no change in the long-term trend which is still bearish for the rand," he added.
He put the near-term technical levels on the upside at 4.61 with medium-term resistance at 4.64.
Another technical analyst, who asked not to be named, agreed. "I see the major longer-term trends in the rand definitely up with targets at the 5.0 level," he said.

The rand's latest strength appeared an over-reaction to the top-side -- a record 4.77 hit at the end of October -- together with support from high interest rates after the Reserve Bank hiked the Bank rate by one percentage point to 17 percent last week.
"After breaking the 4.58 level this (Wednesday) morning, it looks as if we can trade to levels of 4.55, possibly this week. But the longer-term picture has not changed," the analyst said.
He put the medium-term range at 4.50 to 4.63. Beyond that the market was likely to weaken, testing 4.68, then 4.72 and 4.77.
